about: Homework for this pillar, one list per AI (Claude writes it; tools/kit/render.py in jpavia10/prometheus-hub turns it into docs/agents/QUEUE_{ai}.md and the Drive docs). Every task says exactly what to read, what to make, how many, where to save it, how Claude checks it and what makes it not done. A task is done only when the file passes the checks, never because it was sent.

tasks.title: Forge: the function spec, written as the build plan
tasks.why: Owner, 2026-11-16: homework that is legit (it changes what the pillar can do) and detailed enough that it cannot be done wrong.
tasks.unlocks: Joseph goes pillar by pillar, function before form; this file is the plan Claude builds Forge from, step by step.
steps: Open the live page (https://jpavia10.github.io/prometheus-hub/pillars/forge/) on a phone-sized browser and use every section.
Read the code (https://github.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/tree/main/pillars/forge): every file the page loads, and pillar.json.
Write section A from what is there now, with file:line for each item; then B to H.
Write for Claude to build from: exact, testable, nothing vague like 'improve the UX'.

deliver.shape: one markdown file with exactly these headings, in this order: A What it does today | B What Joseph needs it to do | C Data | D Screens | E Rules and edge cases | F Acceptance tests | G Order of work | H Must not

fields.name: A What it does today
fields.rule: every section, control and number on the live page, each with the file and line in the code that makes it (e.g. app.js:142)

fields.name: B What Joseph needs it to do
fields.rule: 'As Joseph, when ..., I want ..., so that ...'; from the pillar's mission and its own data; never invent facts about his life

fields.name: C Data
fields.rule: record | field | type | unit | required | example | storage key (prometheus.<pillar>.<name>) | read by which other pillar

fields.name: D Screens
fields.rule: purpose; every element top to bottom; every number with its formula and source field; the empty state text; the error state

fields.name: E Rules and edge cases
fields.rule: dates and time zones, missing data, offline, two devices, a value of 0 vs unknown

fields.name: F Acceptance tests
fields.rule: Given / When / Then, each checkable in a phone browser in under two minutes

fields.name: G Order of work
fields.rule: each step small enough for one build, with what Joseph can use after it

fields.name: H Must not
fields.rule: the charter's protections that apply, no server or account, no made-up numbers

tasks.example: F7. Given an oil change logged at 12,000 mi and a 6,000 mi interval, when the odometer is set to 17,500 mi, then the service card shows 'due in 500 mi' in amber.
self_check: Every item in A has a file:line that exists.
B has 8+ stories and none invents a personal fact.
C names every field with type and example.
F has 12+ tests, each with one Given, one When, one Then.
G steps are in an order that can ship one by one.
tasks.done_when: 1 file exactly in the shape, every self-check line true.
checks: Claude opens 10 rows (or 10 claims) at random and compares them with their source.

a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
a guess written as a fact (say 'not found' instead)
anything about Joseph's own accounts, balances, mail or records beyond what the task names

tasks.why: Most rejected deliveries fail on things a script can see: wrong name, wrong count, a missing field, a home-page URL, a duplicate row. Today Claude finds them by hand after the fact.
tasks.unlocks: Every AI can run one command on its file before saving, and the Forge can mark a delivery 'shape OK' the moment it lands.
inputs: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/main/docs/agents/queues.json and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/main/pillars/garage/docs/agents/queues.json (the task shape: deliver.file, count, fields)
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/main/proofs/unit/ (how the unit proofs are written: node --test)
steps: Write tools/kit/check_delivery.mjs (Node 20, no dependencies). Usage: node tools/kit/check_delivery.mjs <file> [<task id>]. With no id, find the task whose deliver.file pattern matches the file name ({YYYYMMDD-HHMM} = 8 digits, dash, 4 digits) across docs/agents/queues.json and pillars/*/docs/agents/queues.json.

Checks, each printed as PASS or FAIL with the reason: (1) the file name matches the pattern; (2) a .json file parses; (3) the array length equals count when count > 0; (4) every object has exactly the field names in fields, no more, no fewer; (5) type checks: integer, number, date (YYYY-MM-DD), URL (https, has a path other than '/', not a search page: no 'search', 'q=' or 's=' query); (6) no two rows are equal after lower-casing and trimming every text field except n; (7) any field named quote is 300 characters or fewer; (8) for .md files, every heading the task's shape names is present. Exit code 1 if any check fails.

Write proofs/unit/check-delivery.test.mjs with 12 cases (6 that pass, 6 that each fail one named check) and their fixture files under proofs/fixtures/check-delivery/. Run node --test yourself and paste the output into a comment at the top of the test file.

deliver.file: forge_gemini_check-delivery_{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}.zip (or the three paths as separate files with the same stamp)

self_check: node --test proofs/unit/check-delivery.test.mjs passes on a clean checkout of the repo with your files added.
The script has no dependencies and reads only the repo and the given file.
Running it on garage_gemini_specs (any real delivery) gives a sensible result.
tasks.done_when: Claude adds the files to a checkout and node --test passes 12 of 12, and the checker gives the right verdict on 3 real deliveries from Drive.
checks: Claude runs the tests and the script on 3 real deliveries.
rejected_if: a test that passes because it checks nothing
a dependency or network call
fewer than 12 cases
files saved anywhere but the folder named here
